docs.text: Typical project walkthrough ¶ This page goes through the steps of a typical 3D reconstruction project, from the point cloud to the client deliverables, and the subtleties often met along the way. It also serves as a guide for a first project. 1. Launch CloudCompare, then SEABIM Editor ¶ When CloudCompare starts, a "SEABIM" logo is displayed, showing that SEABIM Editor started correctly. Then open the launcher with the SEABIM icon of the plugins toolbar: The license is checked when the launcher opens. If the workstation is not activated yet, follow the License activation procedure. The launcher opens on the Home tab (see Interface ). 2. Organize the project ¶ 2.1. Working folder ¶ Create the folder structure that gathers every element of the project in a single directory: a folder with the raw data; a folder for the placement plan; a folder, to be kept, with the .bin working session; a folder with the client deliverables. When the team works on a shared folder, everyone creates their project locally with the same folder structure as the shared folder. Folder and file names No spaces or special characters in names: see File formats . 2.2. Save at each milestone ¶ Export tab → Save JSON saves the structure. Save at each project milestone, naming the file according to the structure naming convention , for instance 2026-05-28_14.30.00_mbes_3m3_MAIN_INT_p1_find.json : Milestone When find After automatic detection. filtered After the first filtering. manual_n After each version n of the manual processing. manual_n_AB After version n has been checked by AB (initials). Then copy the JSON to the shared folder. The autosave.json file kept by the launcher does not replace these named saves. 3. The point cloud: bathymetric, LiDAR, photogrammetric ¶ To load a point cloud, drag and drop it onto the CloudCompare window. 3.1. Offset ¶ CloudCompare asks for a project offset: if an offset has already been set for this project, make sure to reuse the same one ; otherwise, choose one close to the working area. Warning: there is one offset per project! Details are given in CloudCompare basics . Finding a project's offset Select a block: the project offset is shown on the Global shift line of the CloudCompare Properties window. 3.2. Point cloud processing ¶ If needed, the point cloud can be processed for smoother work and a better display. 3.2.1. Cut ¶ The point cloud can be cut by block size, by geographic area (trunk, roundhead, etc.) or otherwise. For photogrammetric and bathymetric clouds: first cut the cloud by block size (volume); then split it into sub-parts p1 , p2 , … of 500 meters maximum , for smooth work. Note: keep the full cloud of each zone, before the pX cutting: it is needed for the client deliverable. Mandatory overlap Always keep an overlap between two cut clouds, otherwise processing may produce errors. 3.2.2. Subsample ¶ For very dense photogrammetric data, resampling to 2 cm (0.02 m) is recommended for CloudCompare's smoothness and the computation time of the automatic detection. Bathymetric or LiDAR data do not need resampling. 3.3. Point cloud display ¶ Run the CloudCompare PCV function from the plugins toolbar: Before running these operations The point cloud to process must be selected in the DB Tree . Follow the file naming convention (cutting, resampling, etc.): see File formats . The cut, merge and sampling functions are detailed in CloudCompare basics . 4. 3D model ¶ 4.1. Building a first 3D model ¶ 4.1.1. Find blocks in a point cloud ¶ Import tab → Find blocks in a point cloud (BlockFinder license): The block type and volume are required to run the detection correctly. With two point clouds, run the detection on each one separately: the algorithm is trained specifically for each block type and each cloud type, and differs between photogrammetry and MBES. Several detections can run in parallel, in separate CloudCompare windows. Save the result ( find milestone, see § 2.2 ). Results to be filtered The detection finds the true position of most blocks, but also produces a few misplaced blocks and misses others. Filtering and manual processing are therefore needed (see Processing ). Detection rate The detection rate depends on the quality of the input point cloud. Based on many trials on various projects, the automatic reconstruction rate exceeds 99% on a good photogrammetric cloud, and 95% on a good bathymetric or LiDAR cloud. It is lower on areas of poorer quality, such as the air-water interface or blocks partly hidden behind rock armour. If the rate is low on a standard area, check the quality of the point cloud. 4.1.2. Without automatic detection: add an initial block ¶ Import tab → Load init block : creates the first block of a project. This action is used when automatic detection is not used for a block type, when the license does not include BlockFinder, or to model a block with few features, such as an Accroberm-type toe block. Select the point cloud, then fill in the block type and volume. If the block is not placed at the right spot, it must be moved (see Registration ). The following blocks are created one by one, by duplicating an existing block and registering it (see Adding a missing block ). 4.2. Importing an existing 3D model ¶ 4.2.1. Importing a JSON ¶ Import tab → Load JSON : imports only the 3D structure of an existing model. 4.2.2. Importing a BIN ¶ The whole working session is imported: drag the .bin directly onto the CloudCompare window. 4.3. Importing a second JSON ¶ JSON files sometimes need to be combined, for instance when block placement went on in an area where a first model was built: the new model then completes the first one. Use Load JSON . If the areas overlap, the Merge structures window asks how to resolve conflicts: Keep both blocks ; Priority to new model ; Priority to old model . The distance threshold , expressed as a proportion of the block size, sets how close two blocks must be to count as a duplicate. Points of attention Pay particular attention to the interfaces between different volumes , the waterline , the berm and the toe . If some blocks are not displayed, run Update view ( Ctrl + R ). 5. Block naming ¶ Before the placement plan is loaded, each block carries a unique number assigned by default. For easier handling, the blocks need to be renamed. 5.1. Loading the placement plan ¶ Loading the placement plan of the working area associates each block with a target and a panel. Edit tab → Find names : 5.2. Without a placement plan ¶ To make blocks easier to identify, rename them with a prefix. Select the blocks to rename , then Metadata tab → Rename blocks with prefix (Batch) . Choose a prefix (by area or by volume, for instance) and the starting number: Warning Renaming replaces the panel and the block number: do not apply it to blocks already named from a placement plan. Note: to sort blocks by name, select the folder holding all the blocks, then right click → Sort children by name (A-Z) . 6. Processing ¶ After automatic detection, the structure may hold true blocks but also false ones. The quality control filters highlight them. 6.1. Spotting false or misregistered blocks ¶ After a detection or a registration, the actions of the Quality control module check the consistency and reliability of the model. Overlap and Check for duplicates (nearest neighbor distance) highlight false blocks: overlaps and duplicates. Overlap highlights misplaced blocks that intersect each other. Check for duplicates highlights blocks with a high local density, often duplicates. Compute accuracy and Compute differential (making sure the relevant point cloud is displayed) identify unreliable, hence misregistered, blocks that need particular attention. Here, accuracy and differential highlight misregistered blocks. Note When applying these filters, keeping the 3D model displayed behind helps to see the defects. Recurring errors: duplicates when merging two models with an overlapping area; false blocks from the automatic detection; long and short sides swapped when registering Accropode™ II units. 6.2. Removing false blocks ¶ 6.2.1. Manual filtering ¶ False blocks highlighted by quality control can be removed by hand: Safe delete ( Ctrl + D ): deletes the selected blocks while keeping an undo point; Undo ( Ctrl + Z ) restores them if needed. Deleting directly in CloudCompare ( Del key) is permanent : there is no way back. 6.2.2. Automatic filtering ¶ Right after a detection, a first filtering removes most false blocks. Edit tab → Filter blocks : Three criteria, each one can be turned on or off, quickly sort true and false blocks: Distance : removes overlapping blocks closer than the threshold; Accuracy : removes inaccurate blocks, based on their median score; Point count : removes blocks built on too few points. The Accuracy criterion requires running Compute accuracy first. Filtering does not delete blocks permanently: it can be reverted with Undo ( Ctrl + Z ). Save the result ( filtered milestone, see § 2.2 ). 6.3. Adding a missing block ¶ Select an existing block close to the missing one. Duplicate it with the CloudCompare Clone function. Move it as close as possible to the expected position (make sure to confirm at the end of the move). Register it with Register selection ( Ctrl + E ), see Registration . CloudCompare's basic functions (clone, move, etc.) are covered in CloudCompare basics . If the block exists on the structure but cannot be modeled from the cloud, use Mark missing block instead. 6.4. Registration ¶ To register blocks found by the detection, reworked or added by hand: Select the block and use the CloudCompare move function. Place the block as close as possible to the expected position and confirm the position in the move window: During the move, the Space bar pauses the block, so you can change the viewing angle for a better placement. Run Register selection ( Ctrl + E ). Once registered, the block takes a color reflecting the registration accuracy, from red to green: Here, the block turned dark green: good registration. If the point cloud is noisy, the Custom distance mode of Register selection forces a maximum distance between the block and the cloud. The block must then be moved to its exact position beforehand. Alternatively, Help register opens a panel to translate or rotate the selected block, then registers it on confirmation. If a block stays misplaced, remove it with Safe delete . Warning Only add blocks when their position is certain. 7. Quality control ¶ Quality control is essential to rebuild a 3D model correctly. As detailed above, each filter has its role. 7.1. Compute accuracy ¶ Compute accuracy first gives an idea of the registration accuracy relative to the point cloud. Blocks showing in red and yellow need further registration. When the point cloud is noisy or of lower quality, accuracy drops: blocks along the waterline then stand out. 7.2. Compute differential ¶ Compute differential highlights the differences between the registered 3D model and the point cloud. Areas showing in yellow or red point to a problem and can be re-registered (often misidentified appendices, or long and short sides swapped on Accropode™ II units). Note Hide the 3D model to clearly see the areas showing in red and yellow. 7.3. Check for duplicates ¶ Check for duplicates computes the distance from each block to its nearest neighbor. A red block points to a potential duplicate. To check it, play with the display of the selection: select the block, then press A or V . If a block is still visible, it is a duplicate: one of them can be deleted. 7.4. Overlap ¶ Overlap identifies overlapping blocks. They need particular attention, as they reveal a poor registration, or a broken unit and therefore movement in the area. The Quality control module details these actions. Once the version has been checked, save it ( manual_n_AB milestone, see § 2.2 ). Any remaining corrections go into a new manual_n+1 version. 8. Analysis filters ¶ For the analysis and monitoring of structures, some areas may be more exposed or more sensitive than others, and change over time (settlement, storm, etc.). SEABIM Editor's filters are an aid to analysis and control: they highlight these areas, identify points of interest and make the analysis easier for a specialist. An aid to analysis These are only computation and analysis aid tools: they give a trend, but can in no way give a firm and final conclusion on whether an area is compliant. 8.1. Filter parameters ¶ Filter parameters are edited in Settings ( Ctrl ,). This is where you change, for instance, the expected tolerance for an out-of-profile or for the voids computation. 8.2. Filter results ¶ The filters of the Filters module generate scalar fields. The result is shown on the 3D model at the end of the computation, stored in the metadata of each block, and can be viewed again: with Change color scale ( Ctrl + L ), which also lets you adapt each filter's color scale to the project. Checking Save as default for this scalar field keeps the change on this computer; in the CloudCompare Properties window, Scalar Fields section: the arrow on the right opens the list of the selection's scalar fields. This only works for a single selected block in a working session; in the final render, by changing the display of the whole 3D model in the Properties window, as above; with Show metadata (Block) ( Ctrl + M ), which gathers all the numerical values of the applied filters. Check the console To confirm that a function completed without error, check the console at the bottom of the CloudCompare window: Process finished must appear at the end of the operation, otherwise the error is detailed there. 9. docs.title: Project walkthrough

docs.text: This page goes through the steps of a typical 3D reconstruction project, from the point cloud to the client deliverables, and the subtleties often met along the way. It also serves as a guide for a first project.
docs.title: Typical project walkthrough

docs.text: When CloudCompare starts, a "SEABIM" logo is displayed, showing that SEABIM Editor started correctly. Then open the launcher with the SEABIM icon of the plugins toolbar: The license is checked when the launcher opens. If the workstation is not activated yet, follow the License activation procedure. The launcher opens on the Home tab (see Interface ).
docs.title: 1. Launch CloudCompare, then SEABIM Editor

docs.text: Create the folder structure that gathers every element of the project in a single directory: a folder with the raw data; a folder for the placement plan; a folder, to be kept, with the .bin working session; a folder with the client deliverables. When the team works on a shared folder, everyone creates their project locally with the same folder structure as the shared folder. Folder and file names No spaces or special characters in names: see File formats .
docs.title: 2.1. Working folder

docs.text: Export tab → Save JSON saves the structure. Save at each project milestone, naming the file according to the structure naming convention , for instance 2026-05-28_14.30.00_mbes_3m3_MAIN_INT_p1_find.json : Milestone When find After automatic detection. filtered After the first filtering. manual_n After each version n of the manual processing. manual_n_AB After version n has been checked by AB (initials). Then copy the JSON to the shared folder. The autosave.json file kept by the launcher does not replace these named saves.
docs.title: 2.2. Save at each milestone

docs.text: To load a point cloud, drag and drop it onto the CloudCompare window.
docs.title: 3. The point cloud: bathymetric, LiDAR, photogrammetric

docs.text: CloudCompare asks for a project offset: if an offset has already been set for this project, make sure to reuse the same one ; otherwise, choose one close to the working area. Warning: there is one offset per project! Details are given in CloudCompare basics . Finding a project's offset Select a block: the project offset is shown on the Global shift line of the CloudCompare Properties window.
docs.title: 3.1. Offset

docs.text: If needed, the point cloud can be processed for smoother work and a better display.
docs.title: 3.2. Point cloud processing

docs.text: Run the CloudCompare PCV function from the plugins toolbar: Before running these operations The point cloud to process must be selected in the DB Tree . Follow the file naming convention (cutting, resampling, etc.): see File formats . The cut, merge and sampling functions are detailed in CloudCompare basics .
docs.title: 3.3. Point cloud display

docs.text: JSON files sometimes need to be combined, for instance when block placement went on in an area where a first model was built: the new model then completes the first one. Use Load JSON . If the areas overlap, the Merge structures window asks how to resolve conflicts: Keep both blocks ; Priority to new model ; Priority to old model . The distance threshold , expressed as a proportion of the block size, sets how close two blocks must be to count as a duplicate. Points of attention Pay particular attention to the interfaces between different volumes , the waterline , the berm and the toe . If some blocks are not displayed, run Update view ( Ctrl + R ).
docs.title: 4.3. Importing a second JSON

docs.text: Before the placement plan is loaded, each block carries a unique number assigned by default. For easier handling, the blocks need to be renamed.
docs.title: 5. Block naming

docs.text: Loading the placement plan of the working area associates each block with a target and a panel. Edit tab → Find names :
docs.title: 5.1. Loading the placement plan

docs.text: To make blocks easier to identify, rename them with a prefix. Select the blocks to rename , then Metadata tab → Rename blocks with prefix (Batch) . Choose a prefix (by area or by volume, for instance) and the starting number: Warning Renaming replaces the panel and the block number: do not apply it to blocks already named from a placement plan. Note: to sort blocks by name, select the folder holding all the blocks, then right click → Sort children by name (A-Z) .
docs.title: 5.2. Without a placement plan

docs.text: After automatic detection, the structure may hold true blocks but also false ones. The quality control filters highlight them.
docs.title: 6. Processing

docs.text: After a detection or a registration, the actions of the Quality control module check the consistency and reliability of the model. Overlap and Check for duplicates (nearest neighbor distance) highlight false blocks: overlaps and duplicates. Overlap highlights misplaced blocks that intersect each other. Check for duplicates highlights blocks with a high local density, often duplicates. Compute accuracy and Compute differential (making sure the relevant point cloud is displayed) identify unreliable, hence misregistered, blocks that need particular attention. Here, accuracy and differential highlight misregistered blocks. Note When applying these filters, keeping the 3D model displayed behind helps to see the defects. Recurring errors: duplicates when merging two models with an overlapping area; false blocks from the automatic detection; long and short sides swapped when registering Accropode™ II units.
docs.title: 6.1. Spotting false or misregistered blocks

docs.text: Select an existing block close to the missing one. Duplicate it with the CloudCompare Clone function. Move it as close as possible to the expected position (make sure to confirm at the end of the move). Register it with Register selection ( Ctrl + E ), see Registration . CloudCompare's basic functions (clone, move, etc.) are covered in CloudCompare basics . If the block exists on the structure but cannot be modeled from the cloud, use Mark missing block instead.
docs.title: 6.3. Adding a missing block

docs.text: To register blocks found by the detection, reworked or added by hand: Select the block and use the CloudCompare move function. Place the block as close as possible to the expected position and confirm the position in the move window: During the move, the Space bar pauses the block, so you can change the viewing angle for a better placement. Run Register selection ( Ctrl + E ). Once registered, the block takes a color reflecting the registration accuracy, from red to green: Here, the block turned dark green: good registration. If the point cloud is noisy, the Custom distance mode of Register selection forces a maximum distance between the block and the cloud. The block must then be moved to its exact position beforehand. Alternatively, Help register opens a panel to translate or rotate the selected block, then registers it on confirmation. If a block stays misplaced, remove it with Safe delete . Warning Only add blocks when their position is certain.
docs.title: 6.4. Registration

docs.text: Quality control is essential to rebuild a 3D model correctly. As detailed above, each filter has its role.
docs.title: 7. Quality control

docs.text: Compute accuracy first gives an idea of the registration accuracy relative to the point cloud. Blocks showing in red and yellow need further registration. When the point cloud is noisy or of lower quality, accuracy drops: blocks along the waterline then stand out.
docs.title: 7.1. Compute accuracy

docs.text: Compute differential highlights the differences between the registered 3D model and the point cloud. Areas showing in yellow or red point to a problem and can be re-registered (often misidentified appendices, or long and short sides swapped on Accropode™ II units). Note Hide the 3D model to clearly see the areas showing in red and yellow.
docs.title: 7.2. Compute differential

docs.text: Check for duplicates computes the distance from each block to its nearest neighbor. A red block points to a potential duplicate. To check it, play with the display of the selection: select the block, then press A or V . If a block is still visible, it is a duplicate: one of them can be deleted.
docs.title: 7.3. Check for duplicates

docs.text: Overlap identifies overlapping blocks. They need particular attention, as they reveal a poor registration, or a broken unit and therefore movement in the area. The Quality control module details these actions. Once the version has been checked, save it ( manual_n_AB milestone, see § 2.2 ). Any remaining corrections go into a new manual_n+1 version.
docs.title: 7.4. Overlap

docs.text: For the analysis and monitoring of structures, some areas may be more exposed or more sensitive than others, and change over time (settlement, storm, etc.). SEABIM Editor's filters are an aid to analysis and control: they highlight these areas, identify points of interest and make the analysis easier for a specialist. An aid to analysis These are only computation and analysis aid tools: they give a trend, but can in no way give a firm and final conclusion on whether an area is compliant.
docs.title: 8. Analysis filters

docs.text: Filter parameters are edited in Settings ( Ctrl ,). This is where you change, for instance, the expected tolerance for an out-of-profile or for the voids computation.
docs.title: 8.1. Filter parameters

docs.text: The filters of the Filters module generate scalar fields. The result is shown on the 3D model at the end of the computation, stored in the metadata of each block, and can be viewed again: with Change color scale ( Ctrl + L ), which also lets you adapt each filter's color scale to the project. Checking Save as default for this scalar field keeps the change on this computer; in the CloudCompare Properties window, Scalar Fields section: the arrow on the right opens the list of the selection's scalar fields. This only works for a single selected block in a working session; in the final render, by changing the display of the whole 3D model in the Properties window, as above; with Show metadata (Block) ( Ctrl + M ), which gathers all the numerical values of the applied filters.
